title: Dynamic chromatin tethering of MDC1 regulates genome stability.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Retrieved the full open-access text (177,832 characters) and read the data availability statement verbatim; searched the whole text for 'github', 'zenodo', 'figshare', 'dryad', 'GEO', 'GSE', 'PRIDE', 'BioProject' and 'deposit' and found none; Europe PMC reported no accessions in text and only text-mined UniProt P36970 plus one DOI; the NCBI link scan returned only the PMC record itself (no GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample or dbGaP); a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing; the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice, so even the supplement listing could not be retrieved.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about what was measured: single-particle tracking of HaloTag-labelled MDC1 in U2OS and RPE1 cells (N = 3 biological replicates, at least 20 cells per replicate), focus-formation and recruitment microscopy, DR-GFP homologous recombination assays, immunoblots, and time-to-anaphase live imaging. None of these numeric measurements were opened; they exist only as plotted means in figures.

a1_downloadable.note: The data availability statement says only that raw uncropped gel and blot images are in the supplemental file and that 'All primary data will be made available upon reasonable request by J.C.S.'. That is the textbook available-on-request failure. No repository accession, no code repository, no Zenodo/Dryad deposit exists anywhere in the text or in the NCBI/Zenodo searches, and the supplement listing itself could not be retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reached in detail, but no table of any kind is deposited: the quantities a model might predict (bound fraction, diffusion coefficient, focus intensity, time to anaphase, homologous-recombination efficiency) exist only as bar and dot plots inside figures and would have to be reconstructed by digitising images.

a3_inputs_present.note: No per-cell or per-trajectory feature table is available; the single-particle tracking movies analysed in MATLAB with SLIMfast are not deposited.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the figure legends and methods (diffusion coefficients in square micrometres per second, frame rates in frames per second, exposure in milliseconds), but there is no file in which they could be a column.

a5_enough_rows.note: Read from the paper only: experiments are N = 3 biological replicates with at least 20 cells per replicate per condition, so roughly 60-200 cells per condition across a few dozen conditions. Even if every per-cell value were released, that is hundreds of rows, far under the ~1,500 the checklist requires.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A supplemental PDF of blots would be trivially small, but there is no dataset to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download to compare against the paper's stated replicate counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurements are genuine physical readouts (fluorescence microscopy, single-molecule tracking, flow cytometry), not another model's output, so provenance is not the problem here; availability is.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: there is no released dataset, so no model could be trained or evaluated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-molecule movement features of a repair protein to predict how tightly it sticks to chromatin.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would have used per-trajectory single-particle tracking features of HaloTag-labelled MDC1 (a DNA double-strand-break signalling protein) in human U2OS and RPE1 cells. Number of examples unknown; the paper reports only N = 3 replicates with at least 20 cells each per condition.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a molecule is chromatin-bound or freely diffusing, and the resulting bound fraction per cell. The true answer comes from fitting a two-state diffusion model to microscope movies recorded at 138-198 frames per second.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs doing live-cell single-molecule imaging would get a consistent, model-based way to call binding states across mutants and cell-cycle stages. But none of it is testable here, because the trajectories were never deposited.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: classify single-molecule trajectories of MDC1 as chromatin-bound versus diffusing, and predict the effect of PST-repeat phosphomimetic mutations on bound fraction. Dead on arrival because no trajectory data, no per-cell measurement table and no code were released.

effort.compute_note: Nothing estimated, because there is no dataset to size or load.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement: it says primary data is available on request, which kills it in one minute.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright. The paper is a mechanistic cell-biology study whose data availability statement releases only raw gel and blot images and promises everything else 'upon reasonable request'; no accession, repository deposit or code exists, and the measured quantities live only inside figure plots. Sample sizes (about 20-60 cells per condition) would also fail A5 even if released.
